target: V170 retains the V169 single-target-armature skinning path and rebuilds every lavender edge-trim vertex in a local frame formed by its settled sewn edge tangent and adjacent final skirt-face normal. V169 bound trim offsets using only the edge tangent, so Cloth-folded panels could rotate away from the static surface-normal component and leave visible straight bars. This is a disposable prototype repair; skirt drape, fit, appearance, and release remain unapproved.

requiredPatternComponents.reason: Directly observed in the four-view generated concept: fitted ivory long-sleeve jacket, high collar, one diagonal overlapping chest panel, and small quilted elbow panels. Exact seams, closures, ease, scale, and fit remain unverified.
Directly observed as a short pleated layer over fitted shorts; pleat count, panelization, and attachment remain hypotheses.
Directly visible under the overskirt in front, side, and rear views; waistband and crotch construction are not resolved by the concept image.

researchTrial.method: Validate hash-bound construction inputs, manufacture an editable 3D prototype, and directly review its rendered appearance before completion.
researchTrial.review: The concept shows jacket, overskirt, and shorts appearance; it does not establish sewing order, dimensions, allowance, fabric stretch, avatar fitting, or deformation.

bodyProfileEvidence.evidenceBoundary: Neutral and repository-defined Large body cross-sections only. Reuse is bound to the same byte-identical SiroinoSotai PC FBX; waistline selection, garment ease, collar circumference, shape-key coverage, fit, and motion remain unapproved.

releaseBoundary: Prototype geometry only. Rendered visualAppearanceReview, fit, runtime, and customer release evidence remain unverified and mandatory before release.

shapeKeyTransfer.evidenceBoundary: Transfers only the declared body-size keys from the exact source triangle used for weight mapping. It records source and output mesh evidence; it does not claim smoothness, evaluated fit, Unity import compatibility, or release acceptance.

jacket-sleeves.reason: Direct review of the V167 renders still showed jacket sleeves pulled away from the arms after cloth baking. The current hypothesis is to use the already measured target-body authored weights and armature-only sleeve deformation, while retaining Cloth solely for the overskirt.
jacket-sleeves.evidenceBoundary: For the disposable pose hypothesis, interpolate exact imported target-body authored weights over nearest surface triangles and deform sleeves with the target armature only; jacket sleeves are deliberately excluded from native Cloth. Stage 09 independently recalculates and audits production garment weights. This does not prove sleeve fit, collision safety, motion acceptance, appearance, or release readiness.

jacket-bodice.reason: Sleeve-only skinning created a 7.06 mm divergence at a shared sewn vertex. Connected bodice and collar panels must use the same target skeleton and seam-averaged weights so armscye and shoulder seams remain in one deformation basis.
jacket-bodice.evidenceBoundary: Transfer target-body weights onto connected bodice and collar panels and synchronize each shared canonical sewn vertex to the mean of participating panel weights before posing. These non-cloth pose previews are construction diagnostics only and do not establish fit, garment motion acceptance, appearance, or release readiness.

prototypeSharedSeamAnchor.reason: V166 and V167 Cloth baking moved shared canonical sewn boundaries. Correct only shared canonical seam vertices to their measured pre-solve neutral positions; fail if any individual correction exceeds 15 mm.
prototypeSharedSeamAnchor.evidenceBoundary: The actual pre-restore seam gap, number of changed shared references, maximum and mean per-reference correction, and post-restore gap are recorded. This is a capped prototype seam-continuity operation at the neutral export frame, not a pose-fit, appearance, fabric, or release acceptance.

poseResponseTrial.evidenceBoundary: Prototype-only Blender Cloth timeline with the actual target armature driving the collision body and the shared overskirt waist pins before Cloth evaluation. Posed customer renders continue to use the exported rest-shape skinning path; this trial does not create runtime cloth, and does not prove fit or collision safety.

clothSimulation.evidence: V170 retains the V169 armature/Cloth workflow and Stage 09's single target deformation modifier per exported mesh. Each prototype trim vertex is now reconstructed from its settled canonical sewn edge position and interpolated weight using an orthonormal tangent/transverse/adjacent-face-normal surface frame, so folds in the simulated skirt rotate the piping offset with the panel instead of only around the edge tangent. Actual source-edge binding counts and displacements are measured. This is a disposable geometry hypothesis; it does not grant fit, collision safety, appearance, or release acceptance.
clothSimulation.reason: V169 direct inspection found narrow lavender trim sections reading as detached straight bars across the side/back silhouette. The skin exporter previously rotated each trim offset with its sewn-edge tangent alone; it did not follow the settled panel's changing face normal. V170 stores the authored rest surface normal for each canonical hem edge and transports each trim vertex through the current settled edge's tangent and adjacent-face normal frame. Regenerate the sewn prototype, cached cloth, weights, five views and six poses, then inspect current hashes directly. This remains prototype diagnostics only; the overskirt's crumpled silhouette, body fit, collision safety, appearance, and release are not approved.

frontClosure.construction: Right-front hem crosses center by 40 mm in local pattern coordinates, tapering to zero at the upper opening; left front supplies continuous underlay to center. Existing shoulder and side seams retain their common vertices.
frontClosure.evidenceBoundary: Corrects a cut-away lower front into an actual overlap hypothesis. 40 mm extension and 2 mm spacing are design hypotheses, not avatar-approved ease. Closure anchoring, dynamic overlap separation, trim and final fit remain unverified.

prototypeWeightRegions.evidenceBoundary: V80 keeps the connected-panel profile shared across overskirt panels to preserve seam continuity while reducing thigh attachment to the legs in seated/crouch poses. Uncalibrated prototype hypothesis only.

weightProfile.evidenceBoundary: V146 changes the rest-pose geometry path for the sewn front-lap panels by placing them against measured UpperLeg_L/UpperLeg_R deform surfaces with seam fades. The placement is not shape-key fit, motion, collision, seam, visual, or release evidence.

prototypeWeightRegions.evidenceBoundary: V91 keeps the four shorts panels and gusset on the existing experimental weight profile. The generated surface-copy thigh covers are excluded from that profile so their vertices retain barycentric source-body skin weights. This is an uncalibrated prototype hypothesis and grants no fit or appearance acceptance.

weightProfile.evidenceBoundary: Existing V85 prototype distribution is carried onto the V87 gusset for skinning coverage only; no change to measured behavior is claimed. Seam strain, crotch deformation, weight continuity and pose response remain unverified.

prototypeWeightRegions.evidenceBoundary: V91 transfers each copied thigh-cover vertex from the nearest eligible target-avatar body triangle with barycentric source skin weights, without the shorts-panel weight profile. The shell is only an offset copy of neutral body surface; transfer accuracy in motion, seam continuity, fit and shape-key response remain unverified.
